newsitem.title: USA: TransTexas tests Lauro Lopez well.
newsitem.headline: TransTexas tests Lauro Lopez well.

text.p: TransTexas Gas Corp said on Wednesday that its Lauro Lopez No.2 discovery well in the Fandango South field in Texas tested at 50.1 million cubic feet of natural gas per day.
The well has been flowing to sales since December 25, 1996, at a sustained daily rate of 17.5 million cubic feet of gas per day, TransTexas Gas said.
The sustained rate has a flowing tubing pressure of 8,500 pounds per square inch on a 20/64-inch choke, TransTexas said.
TransTexas said the Lauro Lopez well was drilled to 14,746 feet and completed in a 35 feet net pay zone of the A-2 sand of the Middle Wilcox formation.

The company's Lauro Lopez 3 delineation well has encountered shows in the Middle Wilcox sands above 15,700 feet and is currently drilling towards a deeper secondary prospective horizon, the company said.
